title: Course Completion with Tag Filtering
prompt: You are analyzing completion data from an online learning platform, modeled on open education datasets like those from data.gov and EdX public reports. Each completion record includes a `completion_date_text` stored as VARCHAR (format 'YYYY-MM-DD'), a `course_id_code` that may have leading/trailing spaces, a `completion_tags` array indicating delivery modes (e.g., '{"self_paced", "instructor_led"}'), and a `score_text` stored as VARCHAR. Your task: For all courses with at least one completion tagged 'self_paced' in the second half of 2024 (July 1 onward), calculate the average score (from the numeric interpretation of `score_text`) and the count of distinct learners who completed each course. Filter to courses where the average score exceeds 75.0. Return columns: `course_title`, `avg_score` (rounded to 1 decimal), and `learner_count`. Order by `avg_score` descending, then by `course_title` ascending. Courses with NULL scores should be excluded from average calculations. Any course title should appear in Title Case format.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE courses (course_id VARCHAR(20) PRIMARY KEY, course_title VARCHAR(200), category VARCHAR(50)); CREATE TABLE completions (completion_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, course_id_code VARCHAR(20), learner_id INT, completion_date_text VARCHAR(20), score_text VARCHAR(10), completion_tags TEXT[]);
example_input_data: INSERT INTO courses (course_id, course_title, category) VALUES ('CS101', 'introduction to python', 'Programming'), ('DS201', 'DATA ANALYSIS BASICS', 'Data Science'), ('WEB301', 'advanced web development', 'Web'), ('ML401', 'machine learning fundamentals', 'AI'); INSERT INTO completions (course_id_code, learner_id, completion_date_text, score_text, completion_tags) VALUES ('  CS101', 1001, '2024-07-15', '82', '{"self_paced", "online"}'), ('CS101  ', 1002, '2024-08-10', '78', '{"self_paced"}'), (' DS201 ', 1003, '2024-09-05', '88', '{"self_paced", "instructor_led"}'), ('DS201', 1004, '2024-07-20', '91', '{"self_paced"}'), ('WEB301', 1005, '2024-06-15', '85', '{"self_paced"}'), ('WEB301', 1006, '2024-08-25', '70', '{"instructor_led"}'), ('ML401', 1007, '2024-10-01', NULL, '{"self_paced"}'), ('ML401', 1008, '2024-11-12', '65', '{"self_paced"}');

composite_moves: row-filter (date range + array membership + NOT NULL)
type cast (VARCHAR to DATE, VARCHAR to NUMERIC)

hints: You'll need to join the completions to courses, filter by date and tag presence, then aggregate.
The course_id_code has whitespace that must be cleaned before joining. The completion_date_text must be cast to DATE for comparison. Check if 'self_paced' is in the array.

Use TRIM(course_id_code), cast completion_date_text::DATE >= '2024-07-01', check 'self_paced' = ANY(completion_tags), cast score_text::NUMERIC for averaging (handle NULLs/empty strings with a filter or NULLIF), apply INITCAP to course_title, GROUP BY course, HAVING AVG(score) > 75, and order by avg_score DESC, course_title ASC.
answer_key: SELECT INITCAP(c.course_title) AS course_title, ROUND(AVG(NULLIF(TRIM(comp.score_text), '')::NUMERIC), 1) AS avg_score, COUNT(DISTINCT comp.learner_id) AS learner_count FROM courses c JOIN completions comp ON c.course_id = TRIM(comp.course_id_code) WHERE comp.completion_date_text::DATE >= DATE '2024-07-01' AND 'self_paced' = ANY(comp.completion_tags) AND NULLIF(TRIM(comp.score_text), '') IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_title HAVING AVG(NULLIF(TRIM(comp.score_text), '')::NUMERIC) > 75.0 ORDER BY avg_score DESC, course_title ASC;

_meta.scenario: an online course platform tracking course completion and certification
